brief: An interface layer for GNOME 50 that takes its colours from your wallpaper, at all times: a slim strip, a big clock, cards that go light or dark with the picture. The identity must work on any wallpaper, so the mark has no colour of its own.
criteria: Success: recognisable at 16 px as an extension and tab icon, works in one colour (it will take the wallpaper's), clearly not the old contour-map or island identity.

concepts.name: Dusk
concepts.idea: A solid half disc whose other half dissolves into contour lines: light and dark in one shape, the lines of an isobar map.
rationale: Light and dark in one silhouette, which is exactly what the interface does when the wallpaper changes
Contour lines keep the Isobar name and the old project's idea, without the island pill
Reads at 16 px as a half disc with arcs; three cuts (master, small, favicon) are drawn for each size band
Has no colour of its own: the mark takes the wallpaper's hue

recommendation: Dusk: the one mark that says light, dark and adaptive in a single shape, and survives 16 px.
